key_insight: Machine learning can diagnose degradation mechanisms in simulated lead-free RbSn₀.₅Ge₀.₅I₃ solar cells, but reliable predictions depend strongly on training-data coverage.
engineering_relevance: Replacing Spiro-OMeTAD with CuI raised simulated efficiency from 19.6% to 21.6%, mainly through improved fill factor.
method: Compared surrogate models trained on factorial grids and Latin hypercube samples.
Used temperature- and illumination-dependent open-circuit voltage to classify six degradation mechanisms.
evidence_signal: The diagnostic classifier achieved macro F₁ = 0.938 versus 0.687 for physics rules; grid-trained XGBoost fell from R² = 0.9997 on held-out grid points to 0.58 on independent samples, while Latin hypercube training achieved 0.995.
watch_item: Diagnosis was simulation-based and did not generalize to degradation-mechanism combinations absent from training.
paper_title: Interpretable machine learning diagnosis of degradation mechanisms in lead-free $RbSn_{0.5}Ge_{0.5}I_{3}$ solar cells from temperature- and illumination-dependent electrical measurements
